Vacuum baking is performed to induce outgassing of dissolved sub-surface gases (hydrogen) that can create plasmas that lead to RF breakdown. Conditioning (or processing) involves a series of increasing pulse lengths and energies that “season” the structure prior to full-energy operation by removing particle contaminants, desorbing gases, and vaporizing asperities. However, even with proper baking and conditioning, polishing and cleaning of copper cavity components after fabrication and machining are still very important steps in the process of manufacturing full-scale accelerators. Clean fabrication and assembly processes are known to speed up RF conditioning [22], which can often be a very lengthy and costly part of the installation process. Another concern related to the surface finish and cleanliness of high-gradient structures is the presence of “dark current” induced by high voltages. Dark current is a low-level current that arises under high voltage fields prior to breakdown. Dark current can degrade the performance of high-gradient structures as well initiate breakdown events. A study by Suzuki et al. showed that surface preparation has also been shown to affect dark current emissions [23]. Their conclusion was that distilled water cleaning offered the best protection against dark current emissions, however, more research is likely needed to clarify the connection between specific finish, surface preparation techniques and dark current. Regardless, it can be stated that a cleaner surface will minimize dark current. Given the need for adequate surface smoothness and cleanliness, surface preparation is a critical need for the production of high-gradient structures. This section investigates the requirements and best practices for achieving surface preparation and cleanliness in high-gradient structures. Necessary capital expenditures, equipment, materials, personnel, and laboratory space will be considered. Some conventional chemical and electrochemical cleaning methods will also be discussed. However, the paper in which this chart is presented discusses a cleaning procedure prior to diffusion bonding of the disk stack that consists of vapor degreasing, alkaline soak clean, 5 second etching, ultrasonic in de- ionized water as well as clean alcohol. The parts were stored in new, clean alcohol and dried with filtered nitrogen just prior to diffusion bonding.
